messages.author: 6c928594bcdd6fa5
messages.subject: geom_range strange behavior
parts:
Hello everyone,

i'm trying to plot a beast timetree with 95% HPD bar range. However, it seems that the bar is being plotted in a wrong way (seems like 180° rotated to me) and i'm not sure what i'm doing wrong here.

That's the code i'm using to plot the tree

p <- ggtree(btr.haps.beast, color="grey50", size=1) + xlim_tree(120) + theme_tree2() +
  geom_range(range="height_0.95_HPD", color="blue", alpha=0.6, size=2, branch.length = "height_median") + 
  geom_text2(aes(subset=!isTip, label= height_0.95_HPD, digits = 3, hjust=-.3, vjust=1.2), size=3) + 
  geom_text2(aes(subset=!isTip, label=node, hjust=1.5, vjust=-1), size= 3)
p

I've tried many different combinations with heigh and length values of the tree but no one seems to give the same output as figtree does.

For comparison purposes, i'm sending the same tree plotted using Figtree. I've also added the height_range to nodes in order to better explain my problem,

Thanks in advance,

Pedro

Looking at the data of node 24, the left part is indeed shorter than the right part:

> y$height_0.95_HPD[[24]]
[1] 21.90202 33.03405
> rr = y$height_0.95_HPD[[24]]
> m = y$height_median[24]
> m - rr[1]
[1] 3.288516
> rr[2] - m
[1] 7.843513

You can verify it by opening the tree file with text editor.

Jon
